task: Stage 1 MR1 Workforce Identity core: implement canonical workforce sign-in return targets, credential completion, password recovery, MFA entry UX, and owner activation primitives under the existing identity authority. No permission or AAL2 enforcement changes.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This isolated high-risk transaction changes workforce authentication primitives only. A defect could create an unsafe return target, mix shopper and workforce credential state, break privileged password recovery, or create a second session/MFA authority. Active non-auth entrypoint delegates and parked AAL2 enforcement are explicitly excluded.

acceptanceCriteria: Workforce return targets are normalized by one auth-owned fail-closed helper that permits only /admin, /admin/* and exact /storefront-template-preview paths.
The dedicated workforce login accepts the shared safe workforce return target and WorkforceAuthForm uses the same authority when completing the flow.
Workforce password recovery redirects to a workforce-owned credential completion route rather than shopper AuthForm recovery.
Workforce credential completion accepts invite/recovery modes, requires Supabase callback evidence, updates the Supabase password and re-enters canonical workforce login.
An auth-owned owner-activation primitive can create an eligible owner account and hands an immediate authenticated session back to canonical workforce login.
No active /platform, /fiokom, template-preview or admin invitation delegate is changed in this release unit.
No role, tenant, middleware authorization authority or AAL2 enforcement is added, weakened or activated.
invariants: Supabase Auth remains the only session, password and MFA authority.
Server-owned role and tenant authorities remain unchanged.
Customer AuthForm remains shopper-owned and is not imported by workforce credential completion.
A pre-existing arbitrary Supabase session is insufficient to authorize workforce credential completion without invite/recovery callback evidence.
The Auth Core release diff contains no substantive non-auth authority changes.

failureModes: A crafted protocol-relative or external next target escapes the workforce login origin.
The shared return-target helper accepts the preview-login route and creates an authentication loop.
Password recovery sends privileged users through the shopper credential flow.
An already signed-in shopper manually opens the workforce credential page and changes credentials without invite/recovery link evidence.
Owner activation bypasses the server-side eligibility claim or navigates directly into privileged UI instead of canonical workforce login.
The change accidentally activates the parked AAL2 authorization enforcement or changes role/tenant authority.
The isolated release unintentionally edits a non-auth route and violates the release risk budget.
edgeCases: next=/admin and nested admin URLs with query strings are preserved.
Exact /storefront-template-preview with query parameters is preserved.
Recovery without callback evidence fails closed even when a shopper session already exists.
Invite/recovery with valid Supabase callback evidence can set a password and continue through canonical workforce login.
Owner activation without an eligible claim fails closed.
No active caller is required to consume the new activation/credential primitives until the second release unit.

alternatives.summary: Ship auth primitives and all active route delegator changes together.
alternatives.reason: Release Risk Budget proved 10/5 points across four subsystems; high-risk auth authority must be isolated.

alternatives.summary: Raise or bypass the release risk budget for the combined change.
alternatives.reason: The budget is a canonical production control and the change can be dependency-closed through sequential releases without weakening it.

alternatives.summary: Ship only auth-owned primitives first, then rebase non-auth entrypoint delegators on the verified main.
alternatives.reason: This keeps the high-risk auth release at one substantive subsystem while preserving the already designed convergence path.

specialistReviews.finding: Authentication primitives belong to DOMAIN-IDENTITY; active presentation delegates can consume them in a later release.
specialistReviews.resolution: This unit edits only canonical auth paths plus neutral tests.

specialistReviews.finding: A generic existing session must not be treated as invite/recovery authorization.
specialistReviews.resolution: Credential completion requires explicit Supabase callback evidence before the form becomes ready.

specialistReviews.finding: The combined convergence branch exceeded Release Risk Budget because high-risk auth was mixed with three other subsystems.
specialistReviews.resolution: Auth Core is split into its own release transaction; non-auth delegates remain unchanged until a second unit.

challenge.scenario: An attacker supplies //evil.example or https://evil.example as next.
challenge.finding: A local-looking redirect helper can become an open redirect if origin semantics are ambiguous.
challenge.resolution: Normalize against a fixed local origin and allowlist only canonical workforce destinations.

challenge.scenario: A caller supplies /storefront-template-preview-login or /fiokom as next.
challenge.finding: A broad prefix rule can create a loop or cross into shopper account UX.
challenge.resolution: Allow exact preview runtime path only; reject preview-login and shopper account paths.

challenge.scenario: A workforce user requests password recovery.
challenge.finding: Using shopper recovery would recreate split credential authority.
challenge.resolution: WorkforceAuthForm sends recovery directly to the workforce-owned credential route.

challenge.scenario: A shopper session already exists and the user manually opens flow=invite or flow=recovery.
challenge.finding: Session presence alone does not prove possession of a workforce invite/recovery link.
challenge.resolution: Require matching hash type, PKCE code/token hash, or access/refresh token callback evidence before credential update.

challenge.scenario: An owner activation email is not eligible.
challenge.finding: Client signup without the server owner-claim gate could create an unauthorized owner identity.
challenge.resolution: Activation must call /api/platform/activation and fail closed unless eligible=true.

challenge.scenario: Auth Core work is mistaken for AAL2 authorization enforcement.
challenge.finding: Changing requireAdmin/middleware would alter runtime enforcement before the planned final audit.
challenge.resolution: Those authorities remain read-only; tests prohibit workforceAssuranceSatisfied/AAL2 enforcement in this unit.

challenge.scenario: The high-risk auth release also changes active platform/account/preview/admin delegates.
challenge.finding: That would reproduce the Release Risk Budget violation.
challenge.resolution: The plan envelope excludes all non-auth delegates and the release gate must report 5/5 points with one scored subsystem.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code on the exact plan-only Auth Core head before implementation.
Add deterministic return-target, recovery, credential-evidence and activation source-contract tests.
Run Edit-Time / Reference Sync and Incremental Known Failure Replay after the auth-only implementation commit.
Require Release Risk Budget PASS at 5/5 points with exactly one substantive subsystem.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build.
Require exact-head Completion Truth VERIFIED and lifecycle closure before merging Auth Core to main.

requirements.requirement: Canonical workforce authentication primitives provide safe return targeting, workforce-owned recovery/credential completion and owner activation handoff while existing role, tenant, shopper and parked AAL2 authorities remain unchanged.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Workforce return targets must not escape to external, shopper-account or preview-login routes.
An arbitrary existing customer session must not authorize workforce credential completion without callback evidence.
The Auth Core must continue to use Supabase Auth and existing workforce MFA primitives rather than creating another credential/session authority.
This release must not activate or weaken the parked AAL2 authorization enforcement.

requirements.requirement: The high-risk workforce Auth Core ships as an isolated release transaction within the canonical Release Risk Budget.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The high-risk Auth Core release must not be mixed with substantive non-auth subsystems or exceed the canonical release risk budget.

notes: Release Risk Budget on combined workforce convergence head 9565aee4 proved the implementation was too broad: 10/5 points across four subsystems, while Plan Before Code, Edit-Time Guard and Incremental Replay all passed. This transaction is the required first split: high-risk Auth Core only. The already-developed non-auth platform/account/preview/admin delegators remain on the combined reference branch and will be re-applied from verified main as a second release unit. PR #858 remains parked and AAL2 enforcement is not activated. Sentinel integrity correctly rejected CAP-RELEASE evidence embedded inside the CAP-AUTH completion claim. Release isolation is now modeled as a separate CAP-RELEASE requirement proven by GUARD-RELEASE-RISK; the release gate itself remains mandatory and unchanged. Plan Before Code required explicit implementation evidence and negative verification for the CAP-RELEASE claim; both are bound to GUARD-RELEASE-RISK, whose canonical proof semantics are CAP-RELEASE with risk/release-scope dimensions.
